L307: ## 1.2. Environment variablescite88†¶ L308: 
L309: These environment variables influence Python’s behavior, they are processed before the command-line switches other than -E or -I. It is customary that command-line switches override environmental variables where there is a conflict.
L310: 
L311: `PYTHONHOME`cite39†¶ L312: Change the location of the standard Python libraries. By default, the libraries are searched in `prefix/lib/python version` and `exec_prefix/lib/python version`, where `prefix` and `exec_prefix` are installation-dependent directories, both defaulting to `/usr/local`.
L313: 
L314: When cite39†`PYTHONHOME` is set to a single directory, its value replaces both `prefix` and `exec_prefix`. To specify different values for these, set cite39†`PYTHONHOME` to `prefix:exec_prefix`.
L315: 
L316: `PYTHONPATH`cite38†¶ L317: Augment the default search path for module files. The format is the same as the shell’s `PATH`: one or more directory pathnames separated by cite89†`os.pathsep` (e.g. colons on Unix or semicolons on Windows). Non-existent directories are silently ignored.
L318: 
L319: In addition to normal directories, individual cite38†`PYTHONPATH` entries may refer to zipfiles containing pure Python modules (in either source or compiled form). Extension modules cannot be imported from zipfiles.
L320: The default search path is installation dependent, but generally begins with `prefix/lib/python version` (see cite39†`PYTHONHOME` above). It is always appended to cite38†`PYTHONPATH` .
L321: 
L322: An additional directory will be inserted in the search path in front of cite38†`PYTHONPATH` as described above under cite90†Interface options . The search path can be manipulated from within a Python program as the variable cite6†`sys.path` .
L323: 
L324: `PYTHONPLATLIBDIR`cite91†¶ L325: If this is set to a non-empty string, it overrides the cite92†`sys.platlibdir` value.
L326: 
L327: New in version 3.9.
L328: 
L329: `PYTHONSTARTUP`cite40†¶ L330: If this is the name of a readable file, the Python commands in that file are executed before the first prompt is displayed in interactive mode. The file is executed in the same namespace where interactive commands are executed so that objects defined or imported in it can be used without qualification in the interactive session. You can also change the prompts cite93†`sys.ps1` and cite94†`sys.ps2` and the hook cite95†`sys.__interactivehook__` in this file.

L375: `PYTHONPYCACHEPREFIX`cite80†¶ L376: If this is set, Python will write `.pyc` files in a mirror directory tree at this path, instead of in `__pycache__` directories within the source tree. This is equivalent to specifying the cite70†`-X` `pycache_prefix=PATH` option.

L380: `PYTHONHASHSEED`cite50†¶ L381: 
L382: 
L383: If this variable is not set or set to `random`, a random value is used to seed the hashes of str and bytes objects.
L384: If cite50†`PYTHONHASHSEED` is set to an integer value, it is used as a fixed seed for generating the hash() of the types covered by the hash randomization.
L385: 
L386: Its purpose is to allow repeatable hashing, such as for selftests for the interpreter itself, or to allow a cluster of python processes to share hash values.
L387: 
L388: The integer must be a decimal number in the range [0,4294967295]. Specifying the value 0 will disable hash randomization.

L400: If this is set before running the interpreter, it overrides the encoding used for stdin/stdout/stderr, in the syntax `encodingname:errorhandler`. Both the `encodingname` and the `:errorhandler` parts are optional and have the same meaning as in cite103†`str.encode()` .

L208: Disable the import of the module cite56†`site` and the site-dependent manipulations of cite6†`sys.path` that it entails. Also disable these manipulations if cite56†`site` is explicitly imported later (call cite57†`site.main()` if you want them to be triggered).
L209: 
L210: `-u```cite58†¶ L211: Force the stdout and stderr streams to be unbuffered. This option has no effect on the stdin stream.
L212: 
L213: See also cite59†`PYTHONUNBUFFERED` .
L214: 
L215: Changed in version 3.7: The text layer of the stdout and stderr streams now is unbuffered.
L216: 
L217: `-v```cite60†¶ L218: Print a message each time a module is initialized, showing the place (filename or built-in module) from which it is loaded. When given twice (`-vv`), print a message for each file that is checked for when searching for a module. Also provides information on module cleanup at exit.
L219: 
L220: Changed in version 3.10: The cite56†`site` module reports the site-specific paths and `.pth` files being processed.
L221: 
L222: See also cite61†`PYTHONVERBOSE` .
L223: 
L224: `-W`` arg`cite62†¶ L225: Warning control. Python’s warning machinery by default prints warning messages to cite63†`sys.stderr` .
L226: 
L227: The simplest settings apply a particular action unconditionally to all warnings emitted by a process (even those that are otherwise ignored by default):
L228: 
L229:     -Wdefault  # Warn once per call location
L230:     -Werror    # Convert to exceptions
L231:     -Walways   # Warn every time
L232:     -Wmodule   # Warn once per calling module
L233:     -Wonce     # Warn once per Python process
L234:     -Wignore   # Never warn
L235: The action names can be abbreviated as desired and the interpreter will resolve them to the appropriate action name. For example, `-Wi` is the same as `-Wignore`.
L236: 
L237: The full form of argument is:
L238: 
L239:     action:message:category:module:lineno
L240: 
L241: 
L242: Empty fields match all values; trailing empty fields may be omitted. For example `-W ignore::DeprecationWarning` ignores all DeprecationWarning warnings.
L243: 
L244: The action field is as explained above but only applies to warnings that match the remaining fields.
L355: Changed in version 3.10.15: (also 3.9.20, and 3.8.20) Emits audit events.
L356: 
L357: `PYTHONUNBUFFERED`cite59†¶ L358: 
L359: 
L360: If this is set to a non-empty string it is equivalent to specifying the cite58†`-u` option.
L361: 
L362: `PYTHONVERBOSE`cite61†¶ L363: 
L364: 
L365: If this is set to a non-empty string it is equivalent to specifying the cite60†`-v` option. If set to an integer, it is equivalent to specifying cite60†`-v` multiple times.
L366: 
L367: `PYTHONCASEOK`cite100†¶ L368: If this is set, Python ignores case in cite101†`import` statements. This only works on Windows and macOS.
L369: 
L370: `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE`cite32†¶ L371: 
L372: 
L373: If this is set to a non-empty string, Python won’t try to write `.pyc` files on the import of source modules. This is equivalent to specifying the cite31†`-B` option.
L374: 
L375: `PYTHONPYCACHEPREFIX`cite80†¶ L376: If this is set, Python will write `.pyc` files in a mirror directory tree at this path, instead of in `__pycache__` directories within the source tree. This is equivalent to specifying the cite70†`-X` `pycache_prefix=PATH` option.
L377: 
L378: New in version 3.8.
L379: 
L380: `PYTHONHASHSEED`cite50†¶ L381: 
L382: 
L383: If this variable is not set or set to `random`, a random value is used to seed the hashes of str and bytes objects.
L384: If cite50†`PYTHONHASHSEED` is set to an integer value, it is used as a fixed seed for generating the hash() of the types covered by the hash randomization.
L385: 
L386: Its purpose is to allow repeatable hashing, such as for selftests for the interpreter itself, or to allow a cluster of python processes to share hash values.
L387: 
L388: The integer must be a decimal number in the range [0,4294967295]. Specifying the value 0 will disable hash randomization.
L389: 
L390: New in version 3.2.3.
L391: 
L392: `PYTHONINTMAXSTRDIGITS`cite76†¶ L393: If this variable is set to an integer, it is used to configure the interpreter’s global cite75†integer string conversion length limitation .
L394: 
L395: New in version 3.10.7.
L396: 
L397: `PYTHONIOENCODING`cite102†¶ L398: 
L399: 
L400: If this is set before running the interpreter, it overrides the encoding used for stdin/stdout/stderr, in the syntax `encodingname:errorhandler`. Both the `encodingname` and the `:errorhandler` parts are optional and have the same meaning as in cite103†`str.encode()` .
L401: For stderr, the `:errorhandler` part is ignored; the handler will always be `'backslashreplace'`.
L402: 
L403: Changed in version 3.4: The `encodingname` part is now optional.
L404: 
L405: Changed in version 3.6: On Windows, the encoding specified by this variable is ignored for interactive console buffers unless cite104†`PYTHONLEGACYWINDOWSSTDIO` is also specified. Files and pipes redirected through the standard streams are not affected.
L406: 
L407: `PYTHONNOUSERSITE`cite105†¶ L408: If this is set, Python won’t add the cite53†`user site-packages directory` to cite6†`sys.path` .
L409: 
L410: See also
L411: 
L412: cite54†PEP 370†www.python.org – Per user site-packages directory
L413: 
L414: `PYTHONUSERBASE`cite106†¶ L415: 
L416: 
L417: Defines the cite107†`user base directory` , which is used to compute the path of the cite53†`user site-packages directory` and cite108†Distutils installation paths for `python setup.py install --user`.
L418: 
L419: See also
L420: 
L421: cite54†PEP 370†www.python.org – Per user site-packages directory
L422: 
L423: `PYTHONEXECUTABLE`cite109†¶ L424: If this environment variable is set, `sys.argv[0]` will be set to its value instead of the value got through the C runtime. Only works on macOS.
L425: 
L426: `PYTHONWARNINGS`cite64†¶ L427: 
L428: 
L429: This is equivalent to the cite62†`-W` option. If set to a comma separated string, it is equivalent to specifying cite62†`-W` multiple times, with filters later in the list taking precedence over those earlier in the list.
L430: The simplest settings apply a particular action unconditionally to all warnings emitted by a process (even those that are otherwise ignored by default):
L431: 
L432:     PYTHONWARNINGS=default  # Warn once per call location
L433:     PYTHONWARNINGS=error    # Convert to exceptions
L434:     PYTHONWARNINGS=always   # Warn every time
L435:     PYTHONWARNINGS=module   # Warn once per calling module
L436:     PYTHONWARNINGS=once     # Warn once per Python process
L437:     PYTHONWARNINGS=ignore   # Never warn
